abstract: This study investigated the metabolite profile and biological activities of Zanthoxylum nemorale leaf and stem extracts obtained using hexane, ethyl acetate, and methanol by combining untargeted LC-HRMS metabolomics, multivariate statistical analysis, antioxidant, and antimicrobial assays. A total of 112 metabolites were putatively identified, including coumarins, lignans, flavonoids, alkaloids, phenolic acids, terpenoids, and fatty acids. Methanol extracts exhibited the strongest antioxidant activity, with IC50 values of 53.12 ± 1.11 and 60.70 ± 0.28 µg mL- 1 for stem and leaf extracts, respectively, and showed the highest antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus cereus. Chemometric analyses (PCA, PLS-DA, and hierarchical clustering) clearly discriminated the extracts according to plant organ and solvent polarity. Overall, the extracts were more effective against Gram-positive bacteria than Gram-negative bacteria and fungi. These findings highlight Z. nemorale as a promising source of antioxidant and antimicrobial phytochemicals and demonstrate the value of metabolomics for linking chemical composition with biological activity.
